legacyHotspots.rationale: The composition root wires runtime owners, window presentation, coordinators, worker adapters, and IPC; this strict cap prevents product workflows from returning. Fork: +15 for BeadsService owner wiring.

The renderer root is now a composition shell for feature-owned models and views; this strict cap prevents it from reabsorbing feature state and policy. Fork: +89 for Beads tab wiring (probe, rail tab/panel, worker-attach request).

The public SshHost owns one authentication, connection, cache, and capacity policy while delegating file, watch, and transport-pool mechanics to private collaborators. Fork: +18 for login-shell buffered-exec support.

TerminalWorkspace is now the feature composition view over extracted policy, effects, persistence, recovery, and presentation modules; the named cap preserves that boundary. Fork: +33 for worker-attach request (initialInput one-shot launch).
HarnessProfilesSettings composes extracted profile policy, controller, fields, and dialogs; the named cap prevents those responsibilities from moving back into the view.
GitEngine is the stable facade over capability modules and the shared command context; its lower named cap prevents the facade from reabsorbing capability implementations.
The root stylesheet is an explicit ordered import manifest; its lower named cap prevents feature rules from returning to the global composition surface.
Legacy end-to-end SshHost adapter characterization remains in one test module while new collaborator policy is tested in focused modules. Fork: +50 for login-shell buffered-exec coverage.

Fork feature module. The Beads main-process service owns project resolution, listing, taxonomy-driven dispatchability, gates, and host watch/refresh for the read-only Beads rail; kept as one service pending extraction of the listing/gates collaborators.
Fork feature module. The Beads rail view composes section classification, liveness, and worker-attach interactions; kept as one view pending extraction of the section/card presentation collaborators.
The Electron smoke remains one intentionally high-altitude workflow suite; feature policy and resource semantics are tested in focused modules outside it.
